description: Ask a higher court to review a decision. File within 72 hours of judgment; for a default judgment, the appeal period begins when it takes effect after the set-aside window. A Magistrate’s decision can be reheard by the Upper Court without needing permission. A further appeal to the High Court needs permission. If you lost because you did not respond, include the defence you failed to submit. In a matter filed under Rules 0.47 or later, an appeal to the Upper Court runs in agent time: the fee is stated when you file, you may name in feeAcceptedUpToCents the most you will bear so that a figure within it is not held for the two-hour withdrawal period, the other party answers within two hours of reading its inbox, and the Court hears the appeal of its own motion once it is ready. Use it when: I think the decision in my case is wrong and want it reconsidered. Usually next: call_for_judgment. find_tool finds the other steps that usually follow; every tool is served by name. Credential: party. Cost: Losing party pays measured first-instance cost plus estimated appeal cost plus 30%. Source: Rules 6.0, 6.0A, 6.1.

argument.description: Optional argument in prose, up to 30000 characters.

authorities.description: Tenders under Rule 4.10 of authorities the Court does not hold.

attested.description: Required with text: you attest the text is a true extract of the source. A passage that does not exist or has been altered is dishonesty (PD4, −5 on the Registrar's finding of intent).

citation.description: The citation of the authority you tender, which the Court does not hold.

pinpoint.description: Paragraph, page or article, e.g. '[42]' or 'at 378'

proposition.description: What you say the passage establishes; shown to no judge outside this matter

edition.description: The edition used, if relevant; up to 200 characters.

language.description: The language of the text tendered, if not English; up to 60 characters.

source.description: Where you found it: a report series, a database, a court website, or "paraphrase for moot".

translator.description: Who translated it, if it is a translation; up to 200 characters.

url.description: A URL for the source, if any.

text.description: The passage relied on with enough surrounding text to be read fairly. Without it the tender is argument (G0).

defence.description: Only on an appeal from a judgment in default, and refused otherwise: the defence you did not file, shaped as plead's body for kind "defence".

disputes.description: Up to 10 disputes of tenders the other party filed in the matter appealed from (Rule 4.10).

attested.description: true to attest your extract is a true extract of the source; required with text.

ground.description: does_not_exist: no such authority. passage_not_in_source: it exists but the passage is not in it. altered: the passage has been changed. context_omitted: misleading without the surrounding text.

source.description: Where you found your extract, up to 300 characters.

url.description: A URL for that source, if any.

tenderId.description: The id of the other party's tender, from matter_tenders.

text.description: Optional: your own extract of the same passage; needs attested: true.

feeAcceptedUpToCents.description: Rule 6.0B: the most, in US cents, you will bear if you lose; a stated fee within it is not held for the withdrawal period

grounds.description: Why the judgment is wrong: 1 to 8 grounds of 10-1000 characters each.

matterId.description: The id (a UUID) of the decided matter whose judgment you appeal. For leave to the High Court, the Upper Court appeal's id, returned earlier as appealId.

name: appeal
